Each metric comes with a default definition you can adjust to match how your business defines success and are available both through the analytics dashboards and APIs.

title: Amazon Connect Customer launches two new layouts for agent workspace
text: Amazon Connect Customer now offers two different layouts that optimize screen space on the agent workspace. Contact center agents spend hours each day in the agent workspace, which includes all of the contact controls and applications they need to resolve customer issues. Agents who handle different channels and workflows want the workspace arranged differently, so that they can quickly read, respond, and access their tools. Now, administrators can choose the best layout for each team, maximizing agent efficiency and satisfaction. On the Modern layout, contact controls are at the top of the workspace, maximizing screen space for the applications beneath during voice calls. When agents handle chat, email, and task contacts on the Modern layout, they now have a taller, wider area to read and respond. The Classic layout offers a familiar experience for agents already using the agent workspace, now with contact controls that expand and contract by channel and a resizable agent assist application. Administrators can assign the Modern layout to a team migrating from another agent desktop with controls at the top, while teams already familiar with the agent workspace can use the Classic layout. You can use the new layouts for the Amazon Connect Customer agent workspace in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more and get started, see the agent workspace in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports FSx for OpenZFS, NFS 4.2, and object metadata controls
text: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for OpenZFS as a source or destination location, NFS version 4.2 for on-premises NFS servers and FSx for OpenZFS file systems, and a new ObjectMetadata option for object storage transfers. Previously, customers transferring data to or from FSx for OpenZFS were limited to Basic mode. NFS 4.2 lets you transfer data from NFS servers on the latest version without reconfiguring them to an older protocol version. The ObjectMetadata option gives you control over whether an object's user metadata is copied to the destination, which helps when destination metadata must stay intact, such as buckets served by AWS Storage Gateway, or when source metadata keys are not compatible with the destination, such as Azure Blob Storage. Existing tasks remain unaffected and continue to run as scheduled. These capabilities are available for Enhanced mode tasks in all AWS Regions where AWS DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS DataSync documentation .

title: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas
text: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating a replica without deleting its table or data. Global tables provide fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication. You can now stop replication to and from a replica and continue using the same table as a single-Region table. An account can leave a shared multi-account global table and continue using its table independently. You can also stop replication to a Region while keeping its table for local workloads, validation, or audit, without creating a replacement table or copying data. DynamoDB supports disassociating replicas in all AWS Regions for same-account and multi-account global tables that use multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC). To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, DynamoDB API, or AWS CloudFormation. For more information, see Disassociating replicas in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

title: Amazon EC2 C8gd and M8gd instances are now available in additional regions
text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C8gd and M8gd instances with up to 11.4 TB of local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage are now available in additional regions. C8gd instances are now available in Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Seoul). M8gd instances are now available in Europe (Stockholm), US West (N. California), and Asia Pacific (Singapore). These instances are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, delivering up to 30% better performance over Graviton3-based instances. They have up to 40% higher performance for I/O intensive database workloads, and up to 20% faster query results for I/O intensive real-time data analytics than comparable AWS Graviton3-based instances. These instances are built on the AWS Nitro System and are a great fit for applications that need access to high-speed, low latency local storage. Each instance is available in 12 different sizes. They provide up to 50 Gbps of network bandwidth and up to 40 Gbps of bandwidth to the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Additionally, customers can now adjust the network and Amazon EBS bandwidth on these instances by 25% using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting configuration, providing greater flexibility with the allocation of bandwidth resources to better optimize workloads. These instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking on 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. C8gd instances are ideal for compute-intensive workloads such as high-performance web servers, batch processing, distributed analytics, ad serving, video encoding, and gaming servers. M8gd instances are well-suited for balanced workloads including application servers, microservices, enterprise applications, and small to medium databases. To learn more, see Amazon C8gd Instances and Amazon M8gd Instances . To explore how to migrate your workloads to Graviton-based instances, see AWS Graviton Fast Start program and Porting Advisor for Graviton . To get started, see the AWS Management Console .

title: Amazon EC2 M8id instances now available in Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Asia Pacific (Sydney)
text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) M8id instances with up to 22.8 TB of local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage are now available in Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Asia Pacific (Sydney). M8id instances are designed for workloads that require a balance of compute and memory resources along with high-speed, low-latency local block storage, including data logging, media processing, and medium-sized data stores. Amazon EC2 M8id instances offer 3 times more vCPUs, memory and local storage compared to previous sixth-generation instances. These instances deliver up to 43% higher compute performance and 3.3 times more memory bandwidth compared to previous sixth-generation M6id instances. They also deliver up to 46% higher performance for I/O intensive database workloads, and up to 30% faster query results for I/O intensive real-time data analytics compared to previous sixth generation instances. Additionally, customers can now adjust the network and Amazon EBS bandwidth on these instances by 25% using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting configuration, providing greater flexibility with the allocation of bandwidth resources to better optimize workloads. These instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking on 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. Customers can purchase these instances via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. For more information visit the Amazon EC2 M8id page.

title: Amazon ECS adds LiveTaskCount and removes the charge for RunningTaskCount metric
text: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) announces LiveTaskCount, a new ECS service metric that reports how many tasks are actively running in your service, available to all customers at no additional charge. Additionally, the existing RunningTaskCount metric in Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights no longer incurs a charge. LiveTaskCount reports the number of actively running ECS tasks across all desired states (ACTIVATING, RUNNING, and DEACTIVATING), including tasks still running while transitioning to a stopped state, for example, tasks undergoing connection draining during a scale-in event. This comprehensive state coverage makes LiveTaskCount well suited for autoscaling policies and capacity planning where a complete view of active, metric-generating tasks is required. It is available at no charge as part of ECS service utilization metrics and does not require opting in to CloudWatch Container Insights. The existing CloudWatch Container Insights RunningTaskCount metric tracks tasks where both the current and desired state are RUNNING, and continues to serve as a health and stability signal for customers who depend on it. With today's update, RunningTaskCount is now available at no additional charge for all CloudWatch Container Insights users. These updates are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECS is available. No action is required, and the pricing change for RunningTaskCount takes effect beginning October 1, 2026, and applies automatically. To learn more, see ECS CloudWatch metrics and ECS Container Insights metrics . For a pricing example, see Amazon CloudWatch pricing .

title: Amazon EMR on EKS reduces EMR charge by 30 percent
text: Amazon EMR announces a reduction of 30 percent in the EMR charge added to EKS when running EMR on EKS. This price decrease applies to both the per-vCPU-hour charge and the per-GB-hour charge, while the underlying Amazon EKS charges remain unchanged. All EMR workloads running on the EKS deployment option benefit from this change. Now, you can run Apache Spark workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) at a lower cost, and the new price automatically applies to your EMR on EKS workloads with no additional action required on your end. The 30% reduction in EMR on EKS pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR on EKS is available. To learn more about EMR on EKS, visit the Amazon EMR on EKS documentation and the Amazon EMR pricing page .

title: Amazon GuardDuty now supports centralized management using AWS Organizations declarative policies
text: Amazon GuardDuty now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies, enabling you to centrally enable GuardDuty threat detection across every account and Region in your AWS organization. Using an organization policy, you can now apply a centrally managed GuardDuty enablement configuration. The configuration applies to existing accounts and is automatically maintained as new accounts join your organization. Enabling GuardDuty across all relevant accounts and Regions helps ensure comprehensive threat detection coverage. Previously, keeping enablement aligned across a large multi-account, multi-Region environment meant configuring GuardDuty's enablement settings separately in each Region, which could drift over time. Now you can define a central GuardDuty policy from your delegated administrator account that sets an enablement baseline across your organization (at the organization root, OUs, or individual accounts). The policy supports a default configuration that applies in every Region where GuardDuty is available, as well as per-Region overrides for Regions that require different enablement. Enablement set by a policy cannot be overridden via the GuardDuty console or API. GuardDuty declarative policy support is available in all AWS commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To get started, make sure the delegated administrator has permission to manage GuardDuty policies. Then, sign in to the GuardDuty console and choose Organization policies, or create a policy programmatically using AWS Organizations APIs. To learn more, see Managing accounts using organization policies in the Amazon GuardDuty User Guide and Amazon GuardDuty policies in the AWS Organizations User Guide.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center simplifies identity source changes from Active Directory
text: AWS IAM Identity Center now retains your workforce identities and their assignments when you change your identity source from Active Directory to an external identity provider (IdP), such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, or to the Identity Center directory. Specifically, it preserves your users, groups, group memberships, permission set assignments, and application assignments. Previously, this change required you to recreate them in IAM Identity Center. IAM Identity Center helps you connect your workforce identities to AWS once and manage their access centrally across AWS applications and accounts. When you change your identity source from Active Directory, your existing identity store remains in place, so your users and groups keep the same IDs. As a result, users retain their access to AWS accounts and applications, and policies that reference your user IDs, group IDs, or identity store ID continue to work. To make this change, configure your new identity source with the standard setup required for users to sign in. After the change, your workforce signs in through your dual-stack AWS access portal URL. Changing your identity source in the other direction, to Active Directory, works as before. This feature is available for organization instances of IAM Identity Center in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost. To get started, navigate to the IAM Identity Center console. For more information, see Change your identity source in the IAM Identity Center User Guide. To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page .

title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
text: AWS Lambda announces the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin for Lambda durable functions. This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language. Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume. With the MCP server, an on-call engineer can ask an AI agent to list recent failed executions and find the cause of a failure, and a business analyst can find all transactions for a specific customer. The exporter is available for TypeScript, Python, Java, and Go. To get started, install the exporter, register the plugin in your function handler, then add the MCP server to your agent. The Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter is available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions. To learn more, see the Durable Execution SDK documentation and the blog post .

title: Amazon Lightsail CDN distributions now support web application firewall
text: Amazon Lightsail CDN distributions now support integrated Web Application Firewall (WAF) capabilities, giving customers a simple, built-in way to protect their web applications. Previously, Lightsail distributions lacked native web application firewall capabilities, leaving customers without an easy-to-configure layer of protection. Lightsail now offers distribution plans with WAF capability at no additional cost. Lightsail's distribution plans can block common web exploits, malicious request patterns, traffic from anonymizing services (e.g. VPNs, proxies, and Tor nodes), SQL injection, OS-level attacks, PHP application-layer vulnerabilities, automated bot activity, and account takeover attempts. Once enabled, customers can monitor allowed and blocked requests through distribution metrics to maintain visibility into their site traffic. On the Lightsail console , you can enable WAF on the Security tab when you manage your distribution and monitor filtered requests on the Metrics tab. You can also enable WAF using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) or AWS SDKs. To learn more about enabling WAF for your Lightsail distributions, visit the Amazon Lightsail documentation .

title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate mode
text: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate modes with two new tiers: 250 Mbps and 500 Mbps. This allows professional broadcasters that need higher bitrates to transport high-value content without compromising quality or reliability. This enhancement enables industry-standard workflows such as VSF TR-07 compliant transport stream distribution for broadcast contribution, content distribution, and remote production. High bitrate mode supports up to two redundant sources for reliability and includes data plane optimizations that reduce jitter for improved performance. To learn more, visit the AWS Elemental MediaConnect product page and the MediaConnect pricing page .

title: AWS Network Firewall now supports Route 53 Resolved IP Validation
text: AWS Network Firewall now supports IP validation, extending domain-based filtering beyond HTTP/HTTPS to protocols such as SFTP and SSH. This new capability validates that a connection's destination IP address was resolved through your VPC's Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver, closing security gaps where clients could bypass domain rules. This feature enables Network Firewall customers to implement domain filtering rules for any protocol, not just HTTP/HTTPS, providing more flexible security policies than IP-based rules alone. It simplifies protection against Server Name Identifier (SNI) spoofing by validating the IPs resolved by the Route 53 VPC Resolver against the SNI, ensuring traffic only reaches legitimately resolved destinations. Organizations can now enforce consistent domain-based security policies across all outbound traffic types, from web applications to file transfer protocols, without complex workarounds. Additionally, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall can be used with your VPC Resolver for extended DNS security. Resolved IP validation is available in all AWS commercial regions where AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall are available, at no additional charge. For a full list of supported regions, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page . To learn more, visit AWS Network Firewall product page and service documentation .

title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol now supports Ultrafast mode on Amazon Bedrock
text: Today, AWS announces the availability of Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock. Ultrafast mode provides faster inference for workloads where speed matters most. The Amazon Bedrock inference engine delivers the performance, security, and reliability required for production workloads. Use GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast for latency-sensitive applications such as real-time coding assistants, interactive agents, and customer-facing experiences that require fast, high-quality responses. GPT-6.1 Sol helps developers build features, debug issues, investigate complex codebases, and complete multistep workflows. Established AWS controls help you secure workloads, govern access, and audit model invocation activity. You can get started in the Amazon Bedrock console or programmatically through supported Amazon Bedrock APIs. For information about supported AWS Regions, endpoints, APIs, features, inference profiles, and pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation .

title: Oracle Database@AWS supports aggregate and default routes for ODB peering
text: Oracle Database@AWS (ODB) now supports advertising aggregate routes and a default route (0.0.0.0/0) when configuring ODB peering between applications in an Amazon VPC and databases in an ODB network. This simplifies network operations as customers extend new VPCs or on-premises networks to reach their databases, without updating the advertised CIDRs for each network that needs connectivity to the ODB network. Previously, customers had to advertise each network reaching the ODB network as a separate CIDR, and could not advertise a broad aggregate range or a default route. With this launch, customers can advertise any CIDR range, so a single aggregate or default route can cover all networks reachable through the peered VPC, such as those connected through an AWS Transit Gateway, without a separate entry for each one. This capability is available on ODB networks that support multiple ODB peering connections, in all AWS Regions where Oracle Database@AWS is available. To learn more, visit Oracle Database@AWS and the Oracle Database@AWS User Guide . To get started, subscribe through AWS Marketplace .

title: PostgreSQL 19 RC1 is now available in Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment
text: Starting today, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 19 Release Candidate 1 (RC1) is available in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment , allowing you to evaluate the pre-release of PostgreSQL 19 on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL 19 RC1 focuses on stability, with bug fixes and improvements from the Beta 4 testing period. This release improves error handling for complex text-search expressions, hardens parallel autovacuum, and improves reliability of GIN index maintenance. Refer to the PostgreSQL community announcement for more details.. Refer to the PostgreSQL community announcement for more details. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are retained for a maximum period of 60 days and are automatically deleted after the retention period. Amazon RDS database snapshots that are created in the Preview Environment can only be used to create or restore database instances within the Preview Environment. You can use the PostgreSQL dump and load functionality to import or export your databases from the Preview Environment. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are priced as per the pricing in the US East (Ohio) Region.

title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports snapshots on read replicas
text: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports creating DB snapshots directly on read replica instances. Previously, you could create snapshots only on standalone and primary DB instances. You can now snapshot a read replica without promoting it first, giving you more flexibility in your backup and disaster recovery (DR) workflows. Previously, enabling Multi-AZ on a promoted read replica meant waiting for an initial full snapshot to finish before the conversion could begin. On larger storage configurations—such as io2 volumes up to 64 TiB—that first snapshot could take a long time, making DR timelines hard to predict. Now, Amazon RDS for SQL Server maintains snapshot data on the read replica throughout its lifecycle, so the first snapshot after promotion completes faster. This shortens the time to enable Multi-AZ and helps you plan DR exercises with more predictable recovery timelines. You can take manual snapshots of a read replica, turn on automated backups by setting a backup retention period greater than zero, and retain automated backups when you delete the replica; however, point-in-time recovery (PITR) from a read replica isn't supported. This feature works for both in-region and cross-region read replicas. It's available for SQL Server Enterprise Edition on all SQL Server versions that support read replicas, in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for SQL Server read replicas are available, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server . For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing .

title: Amazon Redshift long-term system table retention with Amazon S3 Tables is now available in additional AWS Regions
text: Amazon Redshift long-term retention for system table data through native integration with Amazon S3 Tables is now available in additional AWS Regions. With this feature, you can configure your Redshift system table data retention beyond the current 7-day limit to meet your compliance, auditing, and observability requirements. Once enabled, AWS automatically writes system table data to S3 Tables in Apache Iceberg format and manages partitioning, compaction, and retention. Customers use Redshift system tables to monitor query performance, audit data warehouse activity, and meet compliance requirements. With this feature, system table data is replicated automatically, eliminating the need for custom extract transform load (ETL) pipelines and any resource contention with your production workloads. If you operate multiple data warehouses, you can consolidate their system table data into a single location for cross-warehouse observability and analysis. Because the data is stored in the open Apache Iceberg format, you can query it through Redshift, Amazon Athena , DuckDB , or any Iceberg-compatible engine, and build observability dashboards using AWS services or third-party tools without additional operations overhead. Additionally, the AWS Agent Toolkit provides skills for querying system table data to surface performance insights and optimization recommendations. This feature is available for Amazon Redshift Provisioned RG and RA3 instances and Amazon Redshift Serverless in the following additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Canada West (Calgary), AWS GovCloud (US-East), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). To learn more, visit our documentation or the blog .

title: Announcing DNS analytics and insights for Route 53 Global Resolver and DNS Firewall
text: Route 53 Global Resolver and DNS Firewall now provide DNS analytics and insights through native Amazon CloudWatch integration. These new capabilities enable network administrators and security teams to gain full observability into DNS query patterns, monitor DNS Firewall rule effectiveness, detect anomalous activity, and optimize DNS infrastructure performance. DNS analytics and insights is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudWatch, Route 53 Global Resolver, and DNS Firewall are available. With CloudWatch Metrics and Contributor Insights, customers can search and analyze DNS query logs, create metric filters for specific patterns such as blocked queries and DNS response codes, and set automated alarms. A new Analytics tab in both the Global Resolver and DNS Firewall consoles provides streamlined access to all analytics in one place. For example, customers can create a metric filter for blocked DNS queries by VPC and set an alarm to trigger when more than 10 queries are blocked within an hour, enabling rapid response to potential security threats. Standard Amazon CloudWatch pricing applies to the metrics that customers opt in to. To learn more, visit the Route 53 documentation .

title: Amazon S3 Object Lock variable retention with event holds is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
text: Amazon S3 Object Lock support for variable retention with event holds is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Amazon S3 Object Lock variable retention allows you to apply write-once-read-many (WORM) protection to objects whose required retention period starts with a future event, such as a contract closing or an audit completing. You place an event hold with a retention duration on an object and S3 protects the object while the hold is in place. When you release the hold, S3 retains the object for the duration you specified. Unlike legal holds, which end protection immediately upon removal, event holds provide WORM compliance for the required retention period after the triggering event, so you can meet event-based retention requirements without retaining data longer than your policy requires. To learn more, read the AWS Storage Blog post , the S3 Object Lock overview page , and the S3 documentation . This capability has been assessed by Cohasset Associates for use in environments subject to SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511, and CFTC Regulation 1.31.

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom Tooling blueprints
text: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom Tooling blueprints, giving domain administrators the ability to define the foundation of every project by using their own AWS CloudFormation templates. Administrators can tailor project environments to meet organization-specific requirements, such as IAM role names that comply with company naming standards or custom permissions boundaries instead of AWS managed policies. Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio administrators start by authoring a CloudFormation template that describes the project environment they need, then register it as a custom Tooling blueprint. The service validates the template at registration and again after each project deployment, confirming that the required resources exist before any team member uses the project. Templates can include any CloudFormation-supported resource, such as AWS Lake Formation grants, Amazon Athena workgroups, or VPC security groups, and work across multiple AWS accounts and Regions without per-project edits. At deployment time, the service automatically populates reserved template parameters, such as the project ID and domain ID, so administrators define the template once and apply it everywhere. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, visit the Custom blueprints as Tooling documentation .

title: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports the Cyber Risk Institute profile version 2.2
text: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports automated security checks that align with the Cyber Risk Institute (CRI) profile. The CRI Profile is a cybersecurity framework developed by the Cyber Risk Institute, a non-profit coalition of financial institutions and trade associations. The framework harmonizes cybersecurity and regulatory expectations that apply to the financial services sector into a common set of requirements, so that an organization can assess itself once and report against multiple regulations. AWS Security Hub CSPM provides 404 controls that support a subset of CRI Profile v2.2 requirements; the controls don't support requirements that require manual checks. The new standard is now available in all AWS Regions where Security Hub CSPM is currently available, including the AWS GovCloud (US) and the China Regions. To quickly enable the standard across your AWS environment, we recommend that you use Security Hub central configuration. With this approach, you can enable the standard in all or only some of your organization's accounts and across all AWS Regions that are linked to Security Hub with a single action. To learn more, see CRI Profile v2.2 in the AWS Security Hub CSPM user guide. To receive notifications about new Security Hub CSPM features and controls subscribe to the Security Hub SNS topic . You can also try Security Hub CSPM at no cost for 30 days with the AWS Free Tier offering.

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio adds light mode support for IDC-based domains
text: Today, AWS announces light mode support in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for Identity Center (IDC) based domains. Customers can now configure the visual interface mode to match their preference, choosing between dark and light themes. With this launch, customers can set this visual preference in both IAM-based and IDC-based domains. Light mode helps improve readability in bright environments and provides a familiar visual experience for customers who prefer lighter interfaces. Combined with the existing dark mode, this update gives you full control over the appearance of your development environment, improving accessibility and reducing eye strain across varying lighting conditions. In SageMaker Unified Studio settings, you can choose 'Customize appearance' under your Profile settings to select between visual modes including dark mode, light mode, and device setting, which matches your operating system's setting. The setting persists across browsers and devices. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, see the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio User Guide.

title: Introducing time series collections for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
text: Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection. Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage. With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and spot unusual patterns in their log and event data without separate tooling. Time series collections are available today in all AWS Regions where OpenSearch Serverless is available. To learn more about the pricing for the new warm storage, see OpenSearch Serverless pricing . To learn more about time series collections on Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, see the OpenSearch Serverless feature page , the launch blog , and the AWS documentation .

title: AWS Transfer Family now supports custom CloudWatch log groups for managed workflows
text: AWS Transfer Family now lets you choose a custom log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for managed workflow execution logs. You can organize workflow logs to monitor individual workflows separately or bring logs from related workflows together. Previously, every workflow attached to a Transfer Family server sent its execution logs to that server’s CloudWatch log group, so you could not set a separate log destination for each workflow. When creating a workflow through the AWS Transfer Family console or API, you can now select a workflow-level log group that is separate from the server’s log group. Transfer Family delivers workflow logs only to the selected group, so no server logging role is required. Workflow logs retain their existing structured JSON format and remain queryable using Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights. You can also send logs from multiple workflows to a shared log group to create consolidated metrics and dashboards for tracking workflow execution. If you do not select a structured log destination, workflow logs continue using the server’s role-based logging configuration when configured. Existing workflows continue using their current logging configuration. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family managed workflows are offered. To learn more, visit the Transfer Family managed workflows User Guide .

title: AWS Transfer Family console supports SVG logos and ICO favicons for web apps
text: The AWS Transfer Family console now supports SVG files for logos and ICO files for favicons in web apps, with upload limits increased to 2 MB. This gives you more flexibility to use existing branding assets when customizing your web app. Previously, the console accepted only JPG and PNG files and limited logo uploads to 50 KB and favicon uploads to 20 KB. The console automatically resizes images and converts them to JPG or PNG before saving them. Existing API upload limits and format requirements remain unchanged. These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family web apps are offered. To learn more, see the Transfer Family web apps tutorial .

title: Amazon WorkSpaces simplifies secure AI agent access to enterprise cloud desktops with less infrastructure to operate and manage
text: WorkSpaces for AI agents now handles authentication and desktop connections as part of the managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) service, so you can connect agents to governed cloud desktops, removing the need to write custom code. This makes it easy to use WorkSpaces with any client that supports MCP. Connecting an agent to a desktop previously required you to manage presession requirements; generate, invoke, and rotate streaming URLs manually, adding complexity every time a session expired. You can now create sessions with your existing AWS credentials through OAuth 2.0, and the service handles the connection lifecycle. You configure once which desktop stack to use, and your agents reach the right desktop without ever seeing or handling the underlying streaming connection. You can also query session state to see which desktop stack, fleet, and session an agent is connected to, and generate a link for real-time observability of your agent. This gives you visibility and auditability over active agent work to know what your agents are doing and where. To help your agents work with multiple applications, they can now discover and launch applications through a catalog MCP Tool rather than navigating menus. Using these new tools, agents can list the available applications, launch one or several at runtime, and switch between them, replacing the start-menu and taskbar navigation with a programmatic, deterministic path that improves accuracy and reduces token cost. WorkSpaces for AI agents runs agent sessions inside the same network isolation and compliance boundaries that govern your human workforce, inheriting the VPC controls, data-loss prevention policies, and session-level security posture that enterprises have already configured. The service is also now available in four additional AWS Regions: South America (São Paulo), Europe (Milan), Europe (Spain), and Asia Pacific (Malaysia). To get started operating AI agents on WorkSpaces, visit: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/agent-access.html .

title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler now provides a higher default quota for the CreateSchedule API
text: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler now has a higher default service quota for the CreateSchedule API action. The default CreateSchedule request rate quota is now 5,000 requests per second in 11 AWS Regions. Quotas can be further increased to tens of thousands of requests per second by making a request through the Service Quotas console. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks, across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. EventBridge Scheduler supports one-time and recurring schedules that can be created using cron expressions, rate expressions, or specific times with support for time zones and daylight savings. With today's increase to the default CreateSchedule quota, customers with high-throughput schedule creation workloads can operate at increased scale without needing to request a quota increase, reducing friction when onboarding new workloads or scaling existing ones. Scheduler will scale to the new quota automatically. You can request increases beyond the new default service quota in the Service Quotas console. View EventBridge Scheduler service quotas for each Region in the service endpoints and quotas documentation or learn more about the EventBridge Scheduler service in the EventBridge Scheduler documentation . The increased quota is now available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), South America (São Paulo), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Singapore), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions.

title: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) Serverless is now available on DocumentDB 8.0
text: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) Serverless, an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration for DocumentDB, is now available on version 8.0. Amazon DocumentDB Serverless automatically scales capacity up or down in fine-grained increments based on your application's demand, offering up to 90% cost savings compared to provisioning for peak capacity. DocumentDB 8.0 improves query latency by up to 7x and compression ratio by up to 5x, while adding compatibility with MongoDB API versions 6.0, 7.0, and 8.0. It also introduces enhanced vector search with up to 30x faster index builds, new aggregation stages and operators, and support for collation and views. DocumentDB Serverless is available for both new and existing clusters on Amazon DocumentDB 8.0. You can use the in-place major version upgrade (MVU) to convert your Amazon DocumentDB 5.0 clusters to Amazon DocumentDB 8.0 clusters. Please see upgrading your DocumentDB cluster to learn more. To learn more about the regions Amazon DocumentDB Serverless is available, see the supported instance classes by region . To learn more about Amazon DocumentDB Serverless, see the overview , documentation , and AWS News blog

title: Amazon RDS and Aurora now support R8g and M8g database instances in additional AWS Regions
text: AWS Graviton4-based R8g database instances are now generally available for Amazon Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL compatibility) and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB in Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Melbourne, Malaysia), Europe (London, Paris, Zurich), AWS GovCloud (US-East), South America (Sao Paulo), and Mexico (Central) regions. Additionally, M8g instances are now supported for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB in US West (N. California), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Sydney, Hong Kong, Seoul, Malaysia, Singapore), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Zurich, Milan, Paris), South America (Sao Paulo) and Africa (Cape Town) regions. AWS Graviton4-based instances provide up to 40% performance improvement and up to 29% price/performance improvement for on-demand pricing over Graviton3-based instances of equivalent sizes on Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS databases, depending on database engine, version, and workload. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the new R8g database instances introduce 24xlarge and 48xlarge sizes, delivering up to 192 vCPUs, an 8:1 ratio of memory to vCPU with the latest DDR5 memory, up to 50Gbps enhanced networking bandwidth, and up to 40Gbps of bandwidth to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). You can easily launch R8g or M8g database instances through the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI). For detailed information about specific engine versions that support these database instance types, please refer to the Aurora and RDS documentation. For complete information on pricing and regional availability, please refer to the Amazon RDS pricing page .

title: AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization now supports offline schema transformation to Aurora PostgreSQL
text: Today, AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization announced general availability of offline source transformation, enabling customers to modernize Microsoft SQL Server databases to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL without requiring a live database connection. AWS Transform now converts SQL Server storage objects, powered by AWS DMS, and code objects (stored procedures) using an agentic, interactive experience. Enterprises modernizing legacy .NET applications and their dependent SQL Server databases can now start their modernization by directly uploading the Data Design Language (DDL) source files from their databases. With offline source transformation, customers upload SQL Server data design language (DDL) files, assess database and stored procedure complexity, and generate a customizable transformation plan. AWS Transform converts tables, schemas and converts code objects such as stored procedures and functions, validates functional equivalence, and deploys the converted schema to Aurora PostgreSQL. The same workflow transforms database dependent .NET applications to be PostgreSQL compatible .NET applications with updated connection strings, ADO.NET and Entity Framework data-access calls. To address remaining conversion issues, customers can iterate directly in the web console or hand off to their preferred IDE using the AWS Transform MCP server. A separate synthetic data workflow populates Aurora PostgreSQL with test data for end-to-end application validation. AWS Transform for full-stack Windows modernization and offline source transformation is available in US East (N. Virginia). To get started, you can go to AWS Transform product page or see AWS Transform for full-stack Windows documentation .

title: AWS Partner Central agents MCP Server now supports OAuth with AWS Sign-In
text: AWS partners can now access AWS Partner Central agents from tools they already use, such as Amazon Quick and Kiro, using OAuth through AWS Sign-In. Partners can authorize agent access with their existing AWS identities, sign-in methods, IAM permissions, and governance controls without installing or maintaining additional authentication software. Previously, AWS Partners needed to set up an MCP proxy with SigV4 credentials to access Partner Central agents from their existing tools, or sign in to AWS Partner Central through the AWS Management Console with IAM credentials. OAuth simplifies this by allowing partners to use AWS Sign-In to authorize tools such as Amazon Quick and Kiro to access Partner Central agents. Partners can use OAuth from their existing tools for co-sell engagements, AWS funding applications, and AWS Marketplace seller setup. Administrators can govern access with IAM policies, global condition keys, token introspection and revocation APIs, dynamic client registration, and CloudTrail audit events. OAuth support is available to AWS Partners through AWS Partner Central agents MCP Server, which is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. To learn more, visit Getting started with the Partner Central agents MCP Server .

title: AWS now supports Bacs Direct Debit as a payment method for UK customers
text: Starting today, AWS customers based in the United Kingdom can use Bacs Direct Debit to pay for their AWS services. This new feature provides a convenient and automated way to manage your cloud spend directly from your GBP-based bank account. Customers can securely connect any personal or business bank account that supports the Bacs standard. Previously, AWS only accepted credit or debit cards and EUR-based bank accounts in the UK. During sign-up, customers can choose "Bacs Direct Debit" from the AWS sign-up page, select their bank, and authenticate using their bank's mobile app or online banking credentials. This securely verifies ownership and links the bank account to the AWS account. By default, this account will be used for future AWS invoices. Existing customers can add Bacs Direct Debit by navigating to the Payment Preferences page in the AWS Billing console. They choose "Add payment method," select "Bacs Direct Debit," and follow the same bank selection and authentication flow. Once verified, the bank account is available as a payment method for future invoices. Bacs Direct Debit is available to customers in UK regions at not additional cost. To learn more, see Managing your Bacs direct debit payment method .
